sentences.text: Pappu Dheemar vs Bhuribai Pal on 9 April, 2025

Bench: J.K. Maheshwari, Aravind Kumar  IN THE SUPREME COURT OF INDIA  CIVIL APPELLATE JURISDICTION  CIVIL APPEAL NOS. OF 2025  (Arising out of SLP (C) Nos. 3638-3640 of 2020)
 PAPPU DHEEMAR & ANR. APPELLANT (S)
VERSUS  BHURIBAI PAL & ORS. RESPONDENT(s)
O R D E R 1) Leave granted.

2) The driver and the owner of the vehicle both have filed the present appeals challenging the findings of pay and recovery recorded by the High Court in the impugned judgment, for the reason that the driver of the vehicle was having a driving license with endorsement LMV-TT(tractor-trolley)
on the date of accident, which deserves to be accepted as valid driving license.

3) Having heard learned counsel for the parties, in the facts, the issue which arise for consideration in this appeal has recently been decided by the NIDHI AHUJA Constitution Bench in the case of M/s.Bajaj Alliance General Insurance Company Limited v. Rambha Devi & CA Nos. /2025 (@ SLP (C) Nos. 3638-3640/ 2020) Others (2024) 1 SCC 818 wherein this Court has observed as thus:
131.

sentences.text:
Our conclusions following the above discussion are as under: -
(I) A driver holding a license for Light Motor Vehicle (LMV) class, under Section 10(2)(d) for vehicles with a gross vehicle weight under 7,500 kg, is permitted to operate a Transport Vehicle without needing additional authorization under Section 10(2)(e) of the MV Act specifically for the Transport Vehicle class.
For licensing purposes, LMVs and Transport Vehicles are not entirely separate classes.
An overlap exists between the two.
The special eligibility requirements will however continue to apply for, inter alia, e-carts, e-rickshaws, and vehicles carrying hazardous goods.

(II) The second part of Section 3(1), which emphasizes the necessity of a specific requirement to drive a Transport Vehicle, does not supersede the definition of LMV provided in Section 2(21) of the MV Act.

sentences.text:
(III) The additional eligibility criteria specified in the MV Act and MV Rules generally for driving transport vehicles would apply only to those intending to operate vehicles with gross vehicle weight exceeding 7,500 kg i.e., medium goods vehicle,
medium passenger vehicle, heavy goods vehicle and heavy passenger vehicle.
(IV) The decision in Mukund Dewangan (2017) is upheld but for reasons as explained by us in this judgment.
In the absence of any obtrusive omission, the decision is not per incuriam, even if certain provisions of the MV Act and MV Rules were not considered in the said judgment.
4) In view of the decision in the case of Rambha Devi (supra), the finding recorded by the High Court stands set-aside.

By allowing these appeals, finding on liability stands modified holding that the licence possessed by driver on the date of accident CA Nos.
/2025 (@ SLP (C) Nos. 3638-3640/ 2020) was valid to drive the vehicle in question

,
therefore, owner, driver and insurer are jointly and severally liable for payment of compensation.
In consequence, insurance company has to indemnify the liability and to pay the compensation as awarded.
The remaining part of the order shall remain undisturbed.
5) Acoridngly, the appeals stand allowed.

Pending application(s), if any, shall stand disposed of.
                    .
